articles.title: Global Markets: Fast-fashion giant Shein shrinks value to up to $27 billion in Hong Kong IPO
articles.excerpt:
Shein is set to launch its Hong Kong IPO with an ambitious goal of raising up to $1.8 billion. However, the company's valuation has plummeted to about 70% below its highs in private markets. Investor appetite is being hampered by slower growth and increased competition. In the offering, cornerstone investors will secure $383 million in shares. Trading is scheduled to start on September 1, amidst rising challenges.

articles.title: Global Markets | Japan's Nikkei weighed down by AI stocks ahead of Nvidia earnings
articles.excerpt:
The Nikkei share average in Japan experienced a downturn as stocks related to artificial intelligence faced mounting pressure due to inflation concerns and geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East. While chip-making firms such as Tokyo Electron reported gains, other AI companies struggled. Anticipation builds around potential interest rate hikes from the Bank of Japan, with Nvidia's forthcoming earnings report seen as pivotal for the tech sector.

articles.title: Govt lifts wheat export ban with immediate effect
articles.excerpt:
In February, the government had allowed limited shipments of wheat. | Photo Credit: REUTERS/AMIT DAVE

The government has lifted the export ban on wheat, including the Durum variety grain, with immediate effect.

The government has allowed exports of wheat flour and other products like maida and semolina, according to notifications of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.

In February, the government had allowed limited shipments of wheat.

"The export policy of wheat....is revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect," one of the notifications stated.

articles.title: Corn rockets to 3-year high as traders eye lower U.S. production
articles.excerpt:
CANBERRA, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Chicago corn futures shot to a three-year high on Monday, after a tour by analysts of U.S. farm regions last week found that crops were in worse condition than many expected.

Wheat futures also rose as tit-for-tat attacks by Russia and Ukraine continued to curtail exports from Black Sea ports. Soybeans fell, but prices were supported by strong export demand for U.S beans.

* The most-traded corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was up 2% at $5.18-3/4 a bushel at 0038 GMT after earlier reaching $5.20, the highest since August 2023.

* CBOT wheat climbed 1.1% to $7.07 a bushel and was within a whisker of July's two-year high of $7.11-1/4.

articles.title: MRPL says no single geography, supplier or route decisive for crude sourcing
articles.excerpt:
Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has said that no single geography, supplier or route is ever decisive for it, as it sources crude from across the globe to meet the requirements of the refinery.

Answering to the queries of shareholders on the impact of West Asia crisis on crude oil sourcing of the company at its 38th annual general meeting, M Shyamprasad Kamath, Managing Director and CEO of the company, said MRPL as a company tries to secure crude supply through deliberate diversification of sourcing regions, suppliers, and shipping routes so that no single geography, supplier or route is ever decisive for it.

articles.title: Hindustan Copper OFS: Government to sell up to 6% stake at  ₹514 per share, 10% below market price
articles.excerpt:
The Indian government has announced its second offer for sale (OFS) this month, this time in Hindustan Copper, the state-run company engaged in copper ore mining and production. The government is looking to sell up to a 6% stake in the company through the OFS at a floor price of ₹514 per share.

The floor price represents a 10.45% discount to Hindustan Copper's closing price of ₹574 on the NSE on Monday. The OFS announcement comes at a time when the stock has staged a strong recovery in August, surging 17% and marking its biggest monthly gain since January.

Considering the floor price, the proposed 6% stake sale is valued at around ₹3000 crore, according to Mint calculations.

articles.title: Positive investments in gold ETFs continue for the fifth week in a row
articles.excerpt:
Inflows into physically backed gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) continued to be positive for the fifth consecutive week, as investors found the price of the yellow metal above $4,500 an ounce attractive.

Data from the World Gold Council (WGC) showed that the US and UK led the investments in gold ETFs last week. Investments in the week ending August 21 were $7.56 billion, while exits were to the tune of $1.18 billion, leaving the inflows net positive at $6.38 billion.

Investors are watching US inflation data and Fed signals at Jackson Hole. Rising gold prices and geopolitical tensions continue supporting demand for gold-backed lending.
